speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you had this rash on your scalp and forehead, and has it been spreading?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your son had any difficulty with hair loss or nail changes, and were these rashes noticed in other family members besides your father?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap) in an infant, likely exacerbated by cold weather and possibly with a familial predisposition to psoriasis.
